zones.name: Inbound receiving
zones.role: Check arriving deliveries against expected identity and condition.
zones.decision: Who accepts damaged or unidentified stock?
zones.boundary: A scanned delivery still needs acceptance.

zones.name: Material store
zones.role: Hold lots with explicit identity, location and availability.
zones.decision: Which stock is eligible for this order?
zones.boundary: Physical presence does not establish availability for use.

zones.name: Preparation and dosing
zones.role: Select and measure ingredients for a fictional batch.
zones.decision: What prevents the wrong lot from entering the process?
zones.boundary: A measured quantity must belong to the approved material and task.

zones.name: Processing line A
zones.role: Transform a fictional product using an ordered sequence.
zones.boundary: Device completion alone does not close the production order.

zones.name: Shared utilities
zones.role: Provide the services needed by multiple work centres.
zones.decision: Which orders are affected by a service constraint?
zones.boundary: A shared resource can limit several lines at once.

zones.name: Maintenance workshop
zones.role: Assess faults and return equipment through a controlled handover.
zones.decision: Who confirms the equipment can return to service?
zones.boundary: Repair completion and production release are separate decisions.

zones.name: Quality review
zones.role: Evaluate samples and record a disposition for a fictional lot.
zones.decision: Who can release the lot and on what basis?
zones.boundary: A test result is evidence for an authorised disposition.

zones.name: Processing line B
zones.role: Show an alternative route with its own capability and capacity.
zones.decision: Can the work move here without changing its requirements?
zones.boundary: An alternative route needs capability and resource confirmation.

zones.name: Operations coordination
zones.role: Coordinate the current shift and investigate exceptions.
zones.decision: Which person or system may act on this exception?
zones.boundary: Visibility across a site does not grant every command permission.

zones.name: Planning and demand
zones.role: Translate business demand into an achievable production commitment.
zones.decision: What must be checked before committing the sequence?
zones.boundary: A desired due date does not prove that execution is feasible.

zones.name: Packing and identification
zones.role: Pack released material and preserve its identity.
zones.decision: Which identity leaves the line on each pack?
zones.boundary: Labels must refer to the right released lot and pack specification.

zones.name: Finished stock
zones.role: Stage traceable finished goods for outbound allocation.
zones.decision: Is the selected pallet eligible for this shipment?
zones.boundary: Stock status, reservation and location are distinct facts.

zones.name: Outbound dispatch
zones.role: Verify an outbound load and record the handover.
zones.decision: Which record confirms what was actually shipped?
zones.boundary: A vehicle leaving is not by itself a reconciled goods issue.

scenarios.title: Order to dispatch
scenarios.summary: Follow a fictional order through planning, execution, quality and delivery.

steps.title: Demand becomes a commitment
steps.text: Check feasibility before confirming the order and due date.

steps.title: Allocate an eligible lot
steps.text: Check identity, status and reservation before picking stock.

steps.title: Verify the addition
steps.text: Compare the scan and measured quantity with the authorised task.

steps.title: Execute within limits
steps.text: The controller runs the permitted sequence; supervision retains context.

steps.title: Make the disposition
steps.text: The quality role interprets results and records release or hold.

steps.title: Preserve identity
steps.text: Link packs to the released lot and the required specification.

steps.title: Reconcile the handover
steps.text: Confirm what left and reconcile the business transaction.

scenarios.title: Wrong material scan
scenarios.summary: A convincing screen must still show where an addition is stopped.

steps.title: A task specifies material
steps.text: The task names an eligible material and lot.

steps.title: A different identity appears
steps.text: A synthetic scan does not match the task.

steps.title: Resolve before continuing
steps.text: Hold the addition and ask the authorised role to investigate.

scenarios.title: Quality hold
scenarios.summary: Explore how a hold crosses the physical and business views.

steps.title: The operation ends
steps.text: Equipment reports the end of its sequence.

steps.title: Disposition remains pending
steps.text: A missing or unacceptable result prevents release.

steps.title: Prevent allocation
steps.text: Keep the lot unavailable until an authorised disposition changes.

scenarios.title: Shared resource outage
scenarios.summary: Trace the consequences of one unavailable service.

steps.title: A service becomes unavailable
steps.text: A synthetic observation indicates the required utility is unavailable.

steps.title: Move to a defined state
steps.text: The engineered response governs the line; the viewer merely describes it.

steps.title: Review commitments
steps.text: Assess affected work and a feasible recovery sequence.

steps.title: Return through handover
steps.text: Record the repair and confirm readiness before restarting work.

scenarios.title: Agent proposes a change
scenarios.summary: Keep recommendation, authorisation and execution distinguishable.

steps.title: A recommendation appears
steps.text: An advisory agent proposes a sequence using a synthetic capacity constraint.

steps.title: A person reviews the consequences
steps.text: Check quality, resources and affected commitments.

steps.title: A command needs a separate path
steps.text: Only the authorised control path may request execution. This lab sends no command.

decisions.title: Blender assets or OIP simulation?
decisions.context: Asset authoring and simulated behaviour solve different teaching needs.
decisions.choice: Keep procedural Three.js geometry for the public baseline. Evaluate Blender as an optional asset pipeline and OIP as a candidate simulation environment.
decisions.evidence: The public lab renders procedural meshes and an SVG fallback. No equal-scene comparison is published here.
decisions.limit: No Blender or OIP code, model, licence or runtime is bundled. The exact OIP project/version and reuse terms must be recorded before integration.
decisions.risk: A richer picture may imply physical accuracy that has not been demonstrated.
decisions.next: Define an equivalent scene, acceptance criteria, authoring effort and runtime budget. Record each candidate’s provenance and licence.

decisions.title: One scenario, distinct responsibilities
decisions.context: A shared event can have several consumers with different authority.
decisions.choice: Keep the viewer and teaching simulator observational. No machine commands or business transactions leave this application.
decisions.evidence: The public source has no runtime connector, endpoint configuration or command API.
decisions.limit: Synthetic event delivery illustrates routing; it does not test a real broker or guarantee delivery.
decisions.risk: Visitors may confuse a plausible animation with an observed or accepted operation.
decisions.next: Require a versioned observation contract and independent acceptance before adding any adapter.

decisions.title: Data before bespoke scenes
decisions.context: The same lesson should survive changes to layout and rendering.
decisions.choice: Represent zones, ownership, flows and scenarios as validated data, with geometry as a projection.
decisions.evidence: The editable JSON and schema are published with the lab.
decisions.limit: This is a teaching schema, not an ISA-95 conformance implementation. Parent hierarchy and interchange importers need further design.
decisions.risk: A site hierarchy can hide shared resources and routes if treated as the complete model.
decisions.next: Review one work-centre extension and its shared resources with practitioners.

decisions.title: Public website, local workspaces
decisions.context: Anyone should be able to open the lab without an account.
decisions.choice: Serve static files on GitHub Pages. Store visitor edits in browser local storage. Share reviewed changes through a public pull request.
decisions.evidence: The app has no authentication, backend, telemetry or remote save operation. Source and dependency notices are included.
decisions.limit: Local saves are specific to this browser and device. Clearing browser data can remove them; export JSON for a portable copy.
decisions.risk: An exported workspace can contain whatever a visitor typed. It must be reviewed before publication.
decisions.next: Keep the release allowlist, content review and licence checks in the contribution workflow.

decisions.title: Open source with an explicit boundary
decisions.context: Publishing a teaching vehicle must not imply that other software or business material is licensed with it.
decisions.choice: Apply MIT to the public lab’s original code, synthetic content and documentation. Retain third-party licence notices separately.
decisions.evidence: Scoped LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt, dependency lockfile and public release review are included.
decisions.limit: The licence covers this directory only; it grants no rights to trademarks, customer material or software outside it.
decisions.risk: A future contribution may bring material its author has no right to publish.
decisions.next: Require authors to identify origins and confirm permission to contribute; review both source and generated output.
